# Setup
## Packages
```{r install/load packages}
list.of.packages <-
  c("tidyverse", "ggplot2", "papeR", "car", "rcompanion", "chron", "vegan", "rstatix", "PerformanceAnalytics", "psych")
new.packages <-
  list.of.packages[!(list.of.packages %in% installed.packages()[,"Package"])]
if(length(new.packages)) install.packages(new.packages)

library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(papeR)
library(chron)
library(vegan)
library(PerformanceAnalytics)
library(psych)
```
## read and tidy data
```{r data download and minor fixes}
data1<-read.csv("2-20-2022_NBWQ_Data.csv")
data1[data1 ==""]<- NA
data1[data1 =="NA"]<- NA
data1<-rename(data1, "Vial#_Turbidity" = "Vial._Turbidity")
data1<-rename(data1, "DO_%" = "DO_.")

tide1<-read.csv("NOAA-MLLW_Tides_minute_2021-22.csv")
tide1<-rename(tide1, "PredictedTide" = "pred")
tide_highlow<-read.csv("NOAA-MLLW_Tides_High-Low_2021-22.csv")
chlA<- read.csv("ZP_ChlorophyllData_TIDY_02-03-2022.csv")

data1
tide1
tide_highlow
chlA
```

```{r unite date & time}
#For sake of simplicity, we will substitute the HOBOtime into the Blank spaces of SampleTime_Water
data1<-data1 %>% 
  mutate(SampleTime_Water = ifelse(is.na(data1$SampleTime_Water), data1$HOBOtime, data1$SampleTime_Water)) %>% 
  unite(col = "Date", Month, Day, Year, sep = "/") %>% 
  unite(col = "DateTime", Date, SampleTime_Water, sep = " ", remove = "FALSE")
  
tide1<-tide1 %>% 
  unite(col = "DateTime", date, time, sep = " ", remove = "FALSE")
tide_highlow<-tide_highlow %>% 
  unite(col = "DateTime", date, time, sep = " ", remove = "FALSE")
```

```{r Fix DateTime For tides and survey data}
data2 <- data1 %>%  mutate(DateTime = format(strptime(DateTime, "%m/%d/%Y %H:%M"))) %>% 
  mutate(DateTime = as.POSIXct(DateTime))
data2 <- data2 %>% mutate(Date = format(strptime(Date, "%m/%d/%Y"))) %>% 
  mutate(Date = as.POSIXct(Date))
tide2 <- tide1 %>%  mutate(DateTime = format(strptime(DateTime, "%m/%d/%Y %H:%M"))) %>% 
  mutate(DateTime = as.POSIXct(DateTime))
#lubridate and POSIXct lack time exclusive object classes, chron must be used instead
tide2$time <- chron(times=t(as.data.frame(strsplit(tide2$time,' '))),format=('h:m:s'))
data2$Date <- as.Date(data2$Date)
tide_highlow2 <- tide_highlow %>%  mutate(DateTime = format(strptime(DateTime, "%m/%d/%Y %H:%M"))) %>% 
  mutate(DateTime = as.POSIXct(DateTime))
```

This code may be getting dropped in the future, Amy told me that it was better to graph date on the x-axis such that the axis contains the full range of dates from begining to end of the sample collection phase

```{r create new TideChange column}
tide2 <- tide2 %>% mutate(TideChange = (PredictedTide-lag(PredictedTide)))
#found and removed 4 outliers for TideChange resulting from disjunction in tides across sampling dates
##  to test for outliers of this type, turn off code below code run unique(tide2$TideChange) and select (number of sample dates)-1 most extreme values
tide2$TideChange[abs(tide2$TideChange) >= 0.1] <- NA
```

```{r merge highlow column to tide2}
tide3 <- merge(x = tide2, y = tide_highlow2[ , c("DateTime", "highlow")], by = "DateTime", all.x=TRUE)
```

```{r fix object classes}
data2$Site <- as.factor(data2$Site) 
data2$Bed_Stability <- as.factor(data2$Bed_Stability)
data2$CurrentDirection <- as.factor(data2$CurrentDirection)
data2$PPFD <- as.numeric(data2$PPFD)
data2$ForelUleColorCategory<-as.integer(data2$ForelUleColorCategory)
```

```{r Make selections for what will be included in joined data frames}
data2<- data2 %>% select(c("Site", "Bed_Stability", "Date", "DateTime", "Turbidity_NTU","Sample_ID",  "CurrentDirection", "Temp_C", "DO_mg.L", "DO_%", "Depth_PAR", "PPFD", "BottomDepth_ft", "VegDepth_ft",  "ForelUleColorCategory"))

tide_final<- tide_final %>% select(c("DateTime", "date", "time", "PredictedTide", "TideChange", "highlow", "Flow"))

chlA2<- chlA %>% select(c("Sample_ID", "F_Value", "ug.L", "Dilution", "CalculatedConcentration_ug.L", "CorrectedConcentration_ug.L"))

```

```{r Join 1}
fieldXchlA_join<- data2 %>% left_join(chlA2, by = "Sample_ID")
fieldXchlA_join$Sample_ID <- as.factor(fieldXchlA_join$Sample_ID)
```
```{r Join 2}
data_join<- fieldXchlA_join %>% left_join(tide_final, by = "DateTime")
```

```[BRAINSTORM]
Turbidity		    ←	Depth	        	Regression	        	Observe if depth may correlate with some other variable ↑ NTU such as current		
Color           ←	tide/depth    	ANOVA(2way???)	    	Indiv assessment of depth impact on color
Chlorophyll     ←	Temperature	    Regression	        	Indiv assessment of Temp impact on chlorophyll
Turbidity		    ←	|tide change|   Regression	        	Indiv assessment of tide change impact on NTU
Light		        ←	Chlorophyll   	Regression		        Indiv assessment of chlorophyll impact on light
Turbidity	    	←	Temp	        	Multiple Regression		Observe impact of environmental variables on turbidity
```

## 1 Is there an association between light availability and eelgrass bed stability? (ANOVA)
```{r Create question dataset}
q1data1 <- filter(data_join, !is.na(PPFD) & data_join$Date != as.POSIXct("2022-02-20")) #I messed up on par readings for this date, going to remove them for now.
```
### Step 1: Check Assumptions
#### 1. Outliers
```{r Outliers-boxplot}
library(ggsignif)
### Plot [designed for 768x576]
ggplot(q1data1, aes(x = Bed_Stability, y = PPFD))+ 
 geom_boxplot()+
 geom_signif(comparisons = list(c("Stable","Transitional")),map_signif_level = c("***"=0.001, "**"=0.01, "*"=0.05))+
 labs(y = "PPFD", x = "Bed stability", caption = "geom_signif() does not seem to be working properly, the significance should be higher even with the baseline ANOVA") +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_text(size = 30), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 20), axis.title.y = element_text(size = 30), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 20))
 
# for some reason the geom_signif doesn't seem to work, even without the blocking effect the p-value should be 0.000408 and get at least ***.

```

#### 2. Normality

```{r Normality shapiro.test}
shapiro.test(q1data1$PPFD)
# p-value > 0.05  ☑
## p-value = 0.08908, going to ignore that for now, it should improve as we get more data provided nothing goes wrong
```

```{r Normality Graph}
qqnorm(q1data1$PPFD)
qqline(q1data1$PPFD)
# looks normal to me  ☑
```

#### 3. homogeneity of variance
```{r HOV plot}
q1mod1 <- aov(PPFD ~ Bed_Stability, data = q1data1)
plot(q1mod1, 1)
```
 
```{r HOV tests—functions}

bartlett.test(PPFD~Bed_Stability, data=q1data1)
q1data1 %>% rstatix::levene_test(PPFD ~ Bed_Stability)

# p-value > 0.05  ☑
```
### Step 2: Build model
#### 1 attempt mixed effects model
```{r Create data set with ID}
q1data2 <- q1data1 %>% mutate(ID = 1:nrow(q1data1))
```
```{r model - 1 within factor}
q1mod2 <- aov(PPFD~Bed_Stability + Error(ID/Bed_Stability), data = q1data2)
summary(q1mod2)
summary(q1mod1) # inclusion of the within factor seems to reduce the models significance

```
```{r model - 1 within 1 between factor}
q1mod3 <- aov(PPFD ~ Bed_Stability + Error(ID/Bed_Stability) + Date, data = q1data2)
summary(q1mod3) # inclusion of within and between variables seems to reduce F-value while increasing P-values, reducing model power and significance.
```
```{r}
# Going to do this anyway even though added factors did not improve model.
with(q1data2, interaction.plot(Date, Bed_Stability, PPFD,
                             #ylim = c(5, 20), lty= c(1, 12), lwd = 3,
                             ylab = "PPFD", xlab = "time", trace.label = "Bed stability"))
```
#### 2 Attempt randomized block design
Sources online conflict on proper ordering of elements in aov().
https://stat.ethz.ch/~meier/teaching/anova/block-designs.html puts block factor before treatment while https://www.statmethods.net/stats/anova.html puts it after
I'm inclined to believe the latter as the former has shows outputs structured in a way not in line with the way R does currently. Testing also revealed that the former method leads aov() to ignore the treatment when reporting with summary(), while the latter method reports data for both variables.

```{r build model - Randomized Block}
q1mod.bl1 <- aov(PPFD ~ Bed_Stability + Site, data = q1data1)
summary(q1mod.bl1)
q1mod.bl2 <- aov(PPFD ~ Site + Bed_Stability, data = q1data1)
summary(q1mod.bl2)
```
Looking at the summery of the first model, we can do a quick check to verify whether blocking was efficient or not. We would like the block factor to explain a lot of variation, hence if the mean square of the block factor is larger than the error mean square. we conclude that blocking was efficient (compared to a completely randomized design). Here, this is the case as 
82671 > 44241
.

```{r Table building [papeR]}
q1table <- anova(lm(PPFD~Bed_Stability + Site,data=q1data1))
q1table
q1table_pretty<-prettify(q1table) # having a bit of difficulty trying to figure out how to get the residual statistics on this thing.
q1table_pretty

```

### Step 4: Output assessment 
```{r degrees of freedom}
nrow(q1data1) # n number of observations
length(unique(q1data1$Bed_Stability)) # k number of groups

# Expected df for Bed_Stability is k - 1
length(unique(q1data1$Bed_Stability)) - 1

# expected df for residuals is n - k
40-2
```

### Step 5: Post-Hoc Test
```{r Tukey Honest Significant Difference Test}
TukeyHSD(q1mod.bl1)
```

## 2 Are tempurature and chlorophyll significantly different between stable and ephemeral sites? (logistic REGRESSION)
### 2b what environmental variables are significantly different betwee stable & transitional sites (mulitple logistic Regression)
In this case bed stability is the binary variable
Multiple logistic regression guide: https://rcompanion.org/rcompanion/e_07.html
see also http://www.med.mcgill.ca/epidemiology/joseph/courses/EPIB-621/logistic2.pdf for multivariate logistic regression.
#### Step 1: tidy your data
```{r}
q2data1 <- select(data_join, -c(Date, Sample_ID, CurrentDirection, Depth_PAR, VegDepth_ft, F_Value, ug.L, Dilution, CalculatedConcentration_ug.L, highlow, date, time, Flow))
```


#### Step 2: Visualize the data
I believe this is what is known as a correlation chart???
```{r}
# for this kind of data visualization everything needs to be in numeric form
## Bed_Stability can be turned into a binary value, but Site has to go
data.num <- select(q2data1, -c(Site, DateTime,`DO_%`))
data.num$Bed_Stability <- as.numeric(data.num$Bed_Stability)
data.num$ForelUleColorCategory <- as.numeric(data.num$ForelUleColorCategory)
# for the sake of legibility, we will be changing names for this data frame

chart.Correlation(data.num,
```

```{r label fix 1: brute force}
#found here https://stackoverflow.com/questions/64934425/how-to-increase-the-size-of-the-name-of-variables-in-performanceanalyticschart
mychart.Correlation <- function (R, method = c("pearson", "kendall", "spearman"), ...){
 
 x = PerformanceAnalytics::checkData(R, method = "matrix")
 if (missing(method)) method = method[1]
 cormeth <- method
 panel.cor <- function(x, y, digits = 2, prefix = "", 
                       use = "pairwise.complete.obs", 
                       method = cormeth, 
                       cex.cor, ...) {
  usr <- par("usr")
  on.exit(par(usr))
  par(usr = c(0, 1, 0, 1))
  r <- cor(x, y, use = use, method = method)
  txt <- format(c(r, 0.123456789), digits = digits)[1]
  txt <- paste(prefix, txt, sep = "")
  if (missing(cex.cor)) cex <- 0.8/strwidth(txt)
  test <- cor.test(as.numeric(x), as.numeric(y), method = method)
  Signif <- symnum(test$p.value, corr = FALSE, na = FALSE, 
                   cutpoints = c(0, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 1),
                   symbols = c("***", "**", "*", ".", " "))
  text(0.5, 0.5, txt, cex = cex * (abs(r) + 0.3)/1.3)
  text(0.8, 0.8, Signif, cex = cex, col = 2)
 }
 
 pairs(x, gap = 0, lower.panel = panel.smooth, upper.panel = panel.cor, ...)
 
}
# this option removes histograms, but will allow larger labels along the diagnal. That being said this isn't the worst thing in the world as the histograms did not seem to use logical bin sizes.
names(data.num) <- gsub(" ", "\n", names(data.num))
mychart.Correlation(data.num,
                  method="spearman",
                  cex.labels = 1.5)
```

```{r correlation test}
corr.test(data.num,
          use = "pairwise",
          method="spearman",
          adjust="none",      # Can adjust p-values; see ?p.adjust for options
          alpha=.05)
```

#### Step 3: Run the logistic regression model
```{r}
# for some reason presence of turbidity greatly reduces model significance, but it's absence creates a number of errors stating 
## Warning in cor.test.default(as.numeric(x), as.numeric(y), method = method) : Cannot compute exact p-value with ties
##Warning: glm.fit: fitted probabilities numerically 0 or 1 occurred Warning: glm.fit: algorithm did not converge

### Create new data frame with all missing values removed (NA’s)
data.omit = na.omit(q2data1)


### Define full and null models and do step procedure

model.null = glm(Bed_Stability ~ 1,
                 data=data.omit,
                 family = binomial(link="logit")
                 )

model.full = glm(Bed_Stability ~ Turbidity_NTU + Temp_C + DO_mg.L + PPFD + BottomDepth_ft + ForelUleColorCategory + CorrectedConcentration_ug.L + PredictedTide + TideChange,
                 data=data.omit,
                 family = binomial(link="logit")
                 )
    
step(model.null,
     scope = list(upper=model.full),
             direction="both",
             test="Chisq",
             data=Data)
```
looks like the winning model is:
glm(formula = Bed_Stability ~ PPFD + DO_mg.L + CorrectedConcentration_ug.L, 
    family = binomial(link = "logit"), data = data.omit)

```{r Final Model & graph}
q2mod<-glm(formula = Bed_Stability ~ PPFD + DO_mg.L + CorrectedConcentration_ug.L, data = q2data1, 
    family = binomial(link = "logit"), na.action(na.omit))

summary(q2mod)
### Plot [designed for 786x576]
par(cex.lab = 1.5, cex.axis = 1.3)
plot(sort(fitted(q2mod)), type = "l", lwd = 2, ylab = "Model Probability", xlab = "Sorted Sample Number")
abline(h = mean(fitted(q2mod)), lty = 2)
abline(v = length(q2mod$fit)/2, lty = 2)
# Neat
```
```{r create pretty table}

q2table_pretty<-prettify(summary(q2mod))
q2table_pretty
```

### 2c How is Photosyntheic Photon Flux Density predicted by other measurements (Multiple Regression)

## 3 How do chlorophyll levels impact light availability in the lower bay? (REGRESSION)

### Step 1: Tidy the data, remove NA values from relevant collumns
```{r}
q3data1 <- data_join %>%
  filter(!is.na(PPFD) & !is.na(CorrectedConcentration_ug.L)) %>% 
  select(c("PPFD", "CorrectedConcentration_ug.L"))
#for the sake of readability
q3data1 <- rename(q3data1, "Chlorophyll" = "CorrectedConcentration_ug.L")
#going to make a version without outliers for the sake of having a normalized data set
q3data2<- filter(q3data1, abs(median(Chlorophyll)-Chlorophyll)
      <= 1.5*IQR(Chlorophyll))
```
### Step 2: visualize the data
```{r}
ggplot(q3data1) + 
  aes(Chlorophyll,PPFD) +
  geom_point()
ggplot(q3data2) + 
  aes(Chlorophyll,PPFD) +
  geom_point()
#relationship appears roughly linear but it is difficult to say. something seems off about outliers as well.
```
### Step 3: Check assumptions
```{r normality test}
shapiro.test(q3data1$Chlorophyll)
shapiro.test(q3data1$PPFD)
# here's to hoping more data-points can fix the lack of normality, for now we will check without outliers
```
```{r Normality test 2}
shapiro.test(q3data2$Chlorophyll)
shapiro.test(q3data2$PPFD)
# p-value > 0.05  ☑
```
```{r homoscedasticity test}
chlo.lm1 <- lm(PPFD ~ Chlorophyll, data = q3data1)
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(chlo.lm1)
#fails to pass this test, lets try removing outliers.
```
```{r Homoscedastity test 2}
chlo.lm2 <- lm(PPFD ~ Chlorophyll, data = q3data2)
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(chlo.lm2)
# Much better.  ☑
```

### Step 4: Testing - Correlation
because we now have both a normal and non-normal dataset, we will do both Spearman's rank test and Pearsons product moment.
```{r Corr test}
ChloCorSpear <- cor.test(q3data1$PPFD, q3data1$Chlorophyll, data = q3data, method = "spearman")
ChloCorPears <- cor.test(q3data2$PPFD, q3data2$Chlorophyll, data = q3data2, method = "pearson")
# for some reason cor.test() does not recognize q3data as numeric. Entering in data$column format seems to work for some reason however...
```
```{r [ρ]}
ChloCorSpear$estimate
rho_spear <- round(ChloCorSpear$estimate, 3)
ChloCorPears$estimate
rho_pears <- round(ChloCorPears$estimate, 3)

```
```{r P-value}
ChloCorSpear$p.value
round(ChloCorSpear$p.value, 3)
#p val = 0.144, that's a shame. we will see how this pans out with more samples.
ChloCorPears$p.value
round(ChloCorPears$p.value, 3)
#according to our data [as of 2/25/2022], PPFD is negatively correlated with chlorophyll-a density (rho(ρ)=-0.462, p-val=0.015)
```
### step 5: Regression analysis
```{r}
summary(chlo.lm1)
summary(chlo.lm2)
```

```{r}
q3table_pretty
```

Simple linear regression analysis was used to test if chlorophyll-a concentration, and thus phytoplankton density,  predicted Photosynthetic Photon Flux Density at the depth of seagrass beds. The results of this regression indicated the two predictors explained 21.3% of the variance (R-squared = 0.2128905, F(1,6) = 14.87, p < 0.05).

## multiplot function
This is the definition of multiplot. It can take any number of plot objects as arguments, or if it can take a list of plot objects passed to plotlist.
```{r Multiple Plot Funciton: multiplot}
# ggplot objects can be passed in ..., or to plotlist (as a list of ggplot objects)
# - cols:   Number of columns in layout
# - layout: A matrix specifying the layout. If present, 'cols' is ignored.
#
# If the layout is something like matrix(c(1,2,3,3), nrow=2, byrow=TRUE),
# then plot 1 will go in the upper left, 2 will go in the upper right, and
# 3 will go all the way across the bottom.
#
multiplot <- function(..., plotlist=NULL, file, cols=1, layout=NULL) {
  library(grid)

  # Make a list from the ... arguments and plotlist
  plots <- c(list(...), plotlist)

  numPlots = length(plots)

  # If layout is NULL, then use 'cols' to determine layout
  if (is.null(layout)) {
    # Make the panel
    # ncol: Number of columns of plots
    # nrow: Number of rows needed, calculated from # of cols
    layout <- matrix(seq(1, cols * ceiling(numPlots/cols)),
                    ncol = cols, nrow = ceiling(numPlots/cols))
  }

 if (numPlots==1) {
    print(plots[[1]])

  } else {
    # Set up the page
    grid.newpage()
    pushViewport(viewport(layout = grid.layout(nrow(layout), ncol(layout))))

    # Make each plot, in the correct location
    for (i in 1:numPlots) {
      # Get the i,j matrix positions of the regions that contain this subplot
      matchidx <- as.data.frame(which(layout == i, arr.ind = TRUE))

      print(plots[[i]], vp = viewport(layout.pos.row = matchidx$row,
                                      layout.pos.col = matchidx$col))
    }
  }
}
```

```{r NBWQ_DailySiteData}
#this plot was designed for WQHD (2560x1440p) resolution
#Also note that the graph was orignially made by pasting the legend with MS paint into a version without the legend to allow consistent graph sizes
multiplot(TE,DO,PPFD,FU,CHLO,NTU, cols = 3)
```
